title: Scheduled Maintenance Coordination and Rollback Runbook
author: Priya Menon
content:
Summary
-------
This runbook documents the standardized process for scheduling planned maintenance windows that touch platform-level infrastructure (k8s clusters, model-serving pools, routing/proxy tiers, and observability pipelines). It covers coordination, communication, pre-checks, maintenance steps, monitoring during the window, rollback criteria and procedures, and post-maintenance validation. Aim: minimize customer-visible impact and ensure fast safe rollback when needed.

Scope
-----
Applies to maintenance that: 
- Modifies runtime components: platform-api, routing-proxy, model-router, batch-ingest-worker, metrics-collector.
- Touches k8s-cluster-prod node pools or autoscaling parameters.
- Deploys changes to Redwood Console dashboards or alerting rules that could mask outages.

Not in scope: routine application code releases handled by product release playbooks; database schema migrations are covered in DB-specific runbooks.

SLOs and impact thresholds
-------------------------
- Planned maintenance should target <5m customer-facing interruption for a single route, and <30m for broader rolling restarts.
- If more than 1% of requests fail (5xx) for 5 consecutive minutes or error rate >= 5x baseline for 2 minutes, follow "Abort and Rollback".
- Latency degradation: p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes -> evaluate abort.

Ownership and participants
--------------------------
- Maintenance Owner: engineer who files the change (must be on the calendar and available during the window).
- Platform Oncall (PagerDuty policy: PLT-Platform-Oncall): responsible for real-time monitoring and executing rollback if needed.
- SRE Runbook Lead: coordinates outbound communications and postmortem.
- Release Manager: approves windows affecting dedicated capacity or enterprise customers.

Pre-maintenance checklist (48–72 hours before)
------------------------------------------------
1. Create Change Request in Change Tracker with start/end times and list of affected services. Include rollback plan and owner contact details.
2. Notify stakeholders: #platform-maintenance Slack, account success for impacted customers, security if config access changes.
3. Verify backups and snapshots are recent: k8s cluster etcd snapshot timestamp, model-router config snapshots, and storage snapshot ids.
4. Run smoke tests against staging: autop-run: ./ci/smoke_tests.sh --env=staging. All smoke tests must pass.
5. Validate runbook availability: print and share runbook link. Ensure Platform Oncall is staffed for the window.

Communication templates
-----------------------
- Slack announcement (48h): "Planned maintenance: platform API rolling restart on 2025-10-21 02:00 UTC. Expected impact: brief per-route restarts; no data loss. Contact Priya Menon."
- Incident start post (at window start): include link to change, start time, estimated end, and monitoring dashboard links.

Pre-deploy preflight (10–30 minutes before)
-------------------------------------------
- Confirm feature flags for new behavior are off.
- Run health checks: curl -sS https://platform-api.prod/health | jq .status (expect "ok").
- Verify metrics pipeline healthy: grafana alert "metrics_ingest_lag > 60s" must be OK.
- Snapshot live traffic baseline: runbook command: ./tools/traffic_snapshot.sh --window=5m --out=/tmp/baseline.json

Maintenance procedures (example: rolling restart of model-router pool)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Place model-router pool in maintenance mode (no new golden traffic routing): POST /admin/model-router/maintenance?mode=drain
2. Drain pod (kubernetes): kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
3. Apply config change: kubectl apply -f deploys/model-router/v2-config.yaml --record
4. Wait for pod readiness: kubectl rollout status deploy/model-router --timeout=10m
5. Run canary traffic: ./tools/canary.sh --service=model-router --qps=5 --duration=3m and validate error <0.5% and latency p95 < baseline*1.5
6. If canary OK, continue the roll; if not, follow Abort and Rollback procedure.

Monitoring & dashboards to watch (during the window)
----------------------------------------------------
- PROD / Platform / Overviews -> "platform-critical" dashboard (Grafana)
- Key panels: platform_api_errors_5m (5xx rate), routing_proxy_5xx_rate, model_router_latencies_p95_ms, k8s_node_ready_count, metrics_ingest_lag_seconds.
- Alerts to watch: "platform-high-error-rate", "model-router-p95-latency-spike", "k8s-node-not-ready".

Abort and Rollback criteria (trigger immediately)
------------------------------------------------
Trigger an immediate abort and execute rollback if any of the following are met:
- 5xx error rate > 1% sustained for 5m or spikes above 5% at any time.
- p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10m.
- Canary failure: canary script reports >0.5% error or 3x p95 degradation.
- Downstream failures: dependent service (e.g., metrics-collector) is reporting critical alerts making health checks unavailable.

Rollback procedure (high-level)
------------------------------
1. Stop further rollouts: pause CD pipeline or set deployment replicas to previous release using kubectl rollout undo deploy/<name> --to-revision=<REVISION>.
2. Reopen routing to previous pool: POST /admin/model-router/switch?target=blue
3. Revert config in k8s: kubectl apply -f deploys/model-router/v1-config.yaml
4. Restore node/snapshot if node-level change caused failure: run restore script: ./ops/restore_etcd_snapshot.sh --snapshot-id=<SNAPSHOT_ID> --cluster=k8s-cluster-prod.
5. Notify stakeholders and open an incident if customer impact exceeded thresholds (see "SLOs and impact thresholds").

Post-rollback verification
--------------------------
- Verify 5xx rate returned to baseline within 10 minutes.
- Confirm p95 latency back to baseline within 30 minutes.
- Manually run customer-facing smoke tests: ./ci/customer_smoke.sh --env=prod.

Post-maintenance validation (on success)
---------------------------------------
- Confirm all pods back to desired state, no pending restarts: kubectl get pods -A | grep CrashLoopBackOff (expect none).
- Confirm observability metrics are steady: metrics_ingest_lag < 30s and no new critical alerts.
- Run regression test suite: ./ci/regression.sh --subset=platform-critical.
- Create short post-maintenance summary in #platform-maintenance including deviations, duration, and any follow-ups.

Escalation flow (if abort escalates to incident)
-----------------------------------------------
1. Platform Oncall creates Incident (PagerDuty: PLT-INCIDENT): link to timeline and attach baseline snapshot.
2. SRE Runbook Lead escalates to Engineering Manager if rollback fails after 30 minutes.
3. For customer-impacting incidents, notify Customer Success Lead and schedule a bridge.

Runbook checklist (quick reference)
----------------------------------
- [ ] Change Request created and approved
- [ ] Stakeholders notified
- [ ] Preflight checks passed
- [ ] Backups/snapshots verified
- [ ] Oncall staffed and ready
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards open
- [ ] Canary tests ready and nominal

Appendix A — Common CLI snippets
--------------------------------
- Health check: curl -fS https://platform-api.prod/health | jq .
- Apply deployment: kubectl apply -f deploys/$SERVICE/$CONFIG -n platform-prod
- Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deploy/$SERVICE --to-revision=$REVISION -n platform-prod
- Check node readiness: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep -v Ready

Appendix B — Table: Change types and approval gates
-----------------------------------------------------
| Change Type                         | Approver (minimum)                      | Customer notice needed? | Typical lead time |
|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|-------------------------|-------------------|
| Non-breaking config tweak           | Maintenance Owner                        | No                      | 24h               |
| Rolling restart (stateless services)| Platform Oncall + Release Manager        | Optional                | 48h               |
| Node pool or OS upgrade             | SRE Lead + Release Manager               | Yes (enterprise)        | 72h               |
| Model weight/quantization change    | ML Infra + Product + SRE Lead            | Yes                    | 5 business days   |
